s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis
salient_findings: Reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
key_facts: Previous treatment with topical antifungal cream showed no improvement
Vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C serologic tests negative

shortlist.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, asymptomatic, reddish-brown skin lesion with peripheral ecchymosis

shortlist.label: Hobnail hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Shares histological features with the case, including vascular channels dissecting collagen bundles and prominent hemosiderin deposits

shortlist.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to the presence of a large, vascular lesion, although the lack of systemic symptoms and negative serologic tests make it less likely

shortlist.label: Tufted angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis given the clinical presentation and histological findings, including the presence of dilated vascular channels and bland endothelial cells

shortlist.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Included due to the presence of a complex, vascular lesion with a prominent network of thin-walled channels, although the clinical behavior and prognosis may differ

raw.rationale: The presence of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation, small dilated vascular channels, and the promontory sign are characteristic features of hobnail hemangioma. Additionally, the vascular channel endothelial cells being positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40, and the low Ki-67 index, support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma
rejected.why: Lack of targetoid appearance and presence of hemosiderin deposits, but not exclusively characteristic

rejected.label: Kaposiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Typically presents with more aggressive features, such as Kasabach-Merritt syndrome, and has a higher Ki-67 index

rejected.label: Tufted angioma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a more nodular appearance and has a higher cellularity

rejected.label: Retiform hemangioendothelioma
rejected.why: Characterized by a retiform vascular pattern, which is not described in the histologic findings
